Former CIA officer Felix Rodriguez sits with Tucker Carlson to tell his life story. Rodriguez took part in the hunt for Che Guevara in Bolivia. A famous 1967 photo shows him near the captured rebel.

Rodriguez explains where the photo was taken and what happened that day. He describes flying in by helicopter with the officer in charge. The talk also covers claims about the death of President Kennedy. It ends with his views on coming elections. The episode is part war memoir and part Cold War history told firsthand. His memories carry the weight of that era.

Surgeon and drug maker Patrick Soon-Shiong joins Tucker Carlson to question cancer care. He has spent fifty years working on cures for the disease. Carlson notes a puzzle that haunts him.

Smoking fell hard in the West, yet cancer rates rose. Soon-Shiong made billions selling firms he built for treatment. The title says the public is lied to about causes and cures. He explains what he thinks doctors miss. The episode gives a wealthy insider's challenge to an industry he knows from the lab to the boardroom. He frames diet and drugs as twin suspects.
